reason: Researched via WebSearch/WebFetch (search results were often mis-dated, so I relied only on clearly dated items). The book is +5.28% since inception vs SPY -0.83%, with max drawdown -4.56% through a week when SPY fell ~4.4% in one day, which is the defensive deep-value mandate working. Leg by leg, nothing is broken. Cigna (Q3 released 11-05) beat with adjusted EPS of $7.98 and raised 2026 guidance to at least $30.60, putting it under 10x at $293.59; it sits -1.6% vs an -18% stop. CVS, the weakest leg at -8.9% vs a -20% stop, beat on 11-04 (adjusted EPS $2.09 vs about $1.65 consensus), Aetna's medical benefit ratio improved to 91.3%, and 2026 guidance rose to at least $8.20. At $83.85 that is about 10x, with a 2027 floor of at least $8.44 already set; the drawdown traces to the 10-08 Star ratings and the tape, not the fundamentals, so this is a hold or even a buy-more on weakness, but not worth a full-book rebuild. XOM and CVX are -7%/-5% in the 11-05 energy-led selloff, but the Hormuz situation still looks unresolved, with Brent last reliably dated around $100+ in October, so the tail-hedge rationale stands and both are far from their -15% stops. PFE, BMY and C are near flat or green. The 25% cash at 4% APY is dry powder after a high-volatility week. A resize (for example, adding to CVS) would reset every entry fill and stop in exchange for a marginal tilt, so I keep the book as registered.
